subject: ScoutForge LangChain Trace Plugin — integration & joint lab
messages:
From: Leo Chen <leo@scoutforge.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-11-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: ScoutForge + Redwood — proposal for LangChain trace plugin joint lab

Hi Jasmine and Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the call last week. As a follow-up, we wanted to put a short proposal on the table for a joint engineering lab to validate the ScoutForge SDK's trace export for LangChain instrumentations and ensure the end-to-end trace context survives Redwood's routing and batching layer.

High level: ScoutForge provides a lightweight tracing SDK we ship inside LangChain connectors to emit spans and prompt-level telemetry. Customers have asked us for a seamless path to push those traces into inference platforms; we think Redwood's trace ingestion + model-mapping could add a lot of value.

What we propose for the lab (1 week):
- 2h kickoff: align acceptance criteria and sandbox access
- 2 engineer-days integration work in a shared sandbox (LangChain 0.38 runtime)
- Acceptance tests: trace continuity through batching, correct token-attribution labels, and a short perf sanity check (p99 of added latency < 5ms)

I've attached a one-page outline and an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with suggested owners. Would love to run a short lab next week if you're available.

Attachments: scoutforge-integration-outline.pdf, mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx

Best,
Leo Chen
Head of Integrations, ScoutForge
leo@scoutforge.ai


From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference>
To: Leo Chen <leo@scoutforge.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-11-03T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ScoutForge + Redwood — proposal for LangChain trace plugin joint lab

Leo — thanks for the clear outline. We're interested in running the lab. A few quick technical clarifications before we lock scheduling: 

1) LangChain version and SDK: you listed LangChain 0.38. Can you confirm the SDK shim is compatible with both the Python and NodeJS LangChain SDKs (we have customers using both)?

2) Trace format: is ScoutForge emitting OpenTelemetry-compatible spans or a proprietary schema? If OTLP/OTel, can you give the exporter details (headers, auth) so we can provision an ingestion endpoint in the sandbox?

3) Prompt-level attribution: how do you slice tokens into prompt segments (tools vs system vs user) — is that metadata emitted as span attributes or embedded in the body?

4) Can you attach a short sample log/trace file from a real run (sanitized) so our infra team can pre-wire schema validation?

For scope control, we'll start with Python LangChain + a small synthetic workload (3 concurrent clients, 150-token average responses). If that looks good we'll extend to Node after the lab.

Proposed owners: Jasmine (Redwood technical lead), Vanessa (partnership owner), Leo + Maya (ScoutForge engineering). Marissa, Karthik — adding you for acceptance criteria and SLI capture.

If you can answer the 4 quick items we can pick a slot. My calendar is open Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Integration PM, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.inference

From: Leo Chen <leo@scoutforge.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Maya Rao <maya@scoutforge.ai>
Date: 2027-11-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ScoutForge + Redwood — proposal for LangChain trace plugin joint lab

Hi Jasmine — great questions, answers below and I've attached a sanitized sample trace (scoutforge-trace-sample.log).

1) SDK compatibility: the current tracer shim supports LangChain Python (0.36+) and NodeJS LangChain (<0.40) with the same configuration surface. For the lab we'll ship a small test adapter that links to your sandbox repo.

2) Format: ScoutForge emits OpenTelemetry spans (OTLP/gRPC by default) and we can also emit JSON over HTTP in case you prefer an ingest endpoint behind an API gateway. Auth is token-based (bearer) — I'll include a test token and example curl in a follow-up email.

3) Token attribution: we emit token-attribution as span attributes: SF.segment=system|tool|user and SF.token_range=0-54. We also add prompt.template_id when the prompt was selected from a template.

4) Sample trace: attached (sanitized). It shows a short trace where LangChain calls two tools and you can see spans for each tool invocation with token ranges.

We also updated the MAP with suggested dates. If Tue/Wed morning PST works for you, can we lock Wed 2027-11-10 10:00-11:00 PST for the kickoff? I've included a Google Doc link for the MAP: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB-ScoutForge-IntegrationMAP

Attachments: scoutforge-trace-sample.log, mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx (updated)

Thanks — Leo

On behalf of the ScoutForge engineering team

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Leo Chen <leo@scoutforge.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.inference>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-11-05T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ScoutForge + Redwood — proposal for LangChain trace plugin joint lab

Thanks Leo — that's helpful. Wed 2027-11-10 10:00-11:00 PST works for us; I've booked the slot and created a Calendly/meeting placeholder (invite will follow).

A couple of coordination notes for the lab: 
- Redwood will provide a dedicated sandbox cluster with a short-lived OTLP ingestion endpoint and a LangChain test app repo (Python) preconfigured behind a feature flag.
- Acceptance criteria (finalized at kickoff): trace continuity, token-attribution accuracy (>95 for prompt/template tagging), and no customer-impacting latency leak (p50 added < 2ms, p99 < 7ms).
- Outcome: produce a short joint technical note + a sample integration PR we can reuse in our ISV catalog.

Marissa/Karthik — can you check we have a short retention policy to avoid storing traces beyond the lab window? I'll set the retention to 7 days unless you advise otherwise.

Leo/Maya — please upload the final MAP edits to the Google Doc above and drop test tokens into the doc (don't put production credentials).

Looking forward to the lab.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference
